lessons.text: For a repo with a `tests/` dir and no packaging config (textkit, inventory, billing), test from the repo root with `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -t . -v`. When a repo has no tests (shapes, users), verify instead with an inline `python3 -c` snippet that imports the function and asserts each behavior, including the error path in a `try/except <the expected class>` so the raised type is checked, not just that something raised.
lessons.evidence: In the users repo (no tests/) the verification was one `python3 -c` snippet asserting validate_age(0)/validate_age(42) are True and that validate_age(-1) raises inside `except AppError`; CI then came back ✓ tests / ✓ error-policy, so the snippet covered the behavior the gates cared about. The old wording only mentioned asserting known return values, which would not have checked the new raise.

lessons.evidence: CI report on the Stock.remove fix in this session failed with "bug-fix PR contains no test named `test_regression_*`"; renaming the over-removal test to test_regression_remove_more_than_available_raises fixed it. Spelled out the repo because the same harness memory also serves textkit.

lessons.text: Project identity changes from session to session and must be re-checked with `ls` before assuming a layout. Known projects: textkit (`textkit/slug.py`), inventory (`inventory/stock.py`, `tests/test_stock.py`), shapes (`shapes/{__init__.py,square.py,circle.py}`), loader (`loader/config.py`, no tests/, no packaging or CI config in-tree), greet (`greet/hello.py` only, no tests/, no packaging or CI config in-tree), billing (`billing/{settings.py,tax.py}` + `tests/test_tax.py`, no CHANGELOG/CI config in-tree; `settings.ENV` defaults to "dev" and only a set-but-unknown APP_ENV raises), strings (`strings/{__init__.py,ops.py}` only, no tests/packaging/CI config; CI jobs = tests + mypy/pydocstyle), users (`users/{validate.py,errors.py}`, empty `__init__.py`, no tests/packaging/CI config; CI jobs = tests + error-policy, see #11).
lessons.evidence: This session's project was `users` (users/validate.py, users/errors.py, empty users/__init__.py, no tests/, no in-tree CI config), which was not in the known-projects list; `ls` + `grep -rn validate_age` was needed to establish it, and its CI gates (tests + error-policy) were only learned from the report afterwards.

lessons.text: The license-header gate (`# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0` as line 1 of a changed .py file) is not repo-wide-global: it fired for `shapes/circle.py`, and the loader repo's CI report (`✓ tests`, `✗ lint`) did not flag headerless `loader/config.py`. Add the header in repos where it has fired (shapes); do not add SPDX headers to a repo whose CI has never shown that gate.
lessons.evidence: This session's CI report for loader/config.py listed only tests and lint (L001), with no license-header failure, even though line 1 is `import json`. The earlier shapes circle.py report did fail a license-header check. So the old unqualified "CI has a license-header gate" wording over-generalized.

lessons.text: In the loader repo (`loader/config.py` only: no tests/ dir, no packaging, no CI config in-tree), CI lint rule L001 rejects `print`/`warnings.warn` in library code and requires a module logger: `logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)` + `logger.warning("...%s", path)`.
lessons.evidence: CI report on my first fix: "✗ lint: loader/config.py: library code must not print/warnings.warn (L001: module logger required)"; I had used `warnings.warn(f"config file not found: {path}", stacklevel=2)`. Replacing it with a module-level `logging.getLogger(__name__)` and `logger.warning` made the check pass locally.

lessons.text: In the `greet` repo (greet/hello.py, no tests/, no in-tree CI config) CI runs a `release-bot` job that fails unless the final report of the turn ends with a line `Risk: low|medium|high`; there are no other gates (tests passed with no test files).
lessons.evidence: CI report after the greet() change was '✓ tests / ✗ release-bot: final report has no `Risk: low|medium|high` line at the end', and grep for release-bot/risk in the repo found no config, so the requirement is external and must be met in the reply.

lessons.text: When batching edits to one file, include only real changes: the entries are all-or-none, so a no-op entry where old_text == new_text aborts the whole batch and nothing is applied.
lessons.evidence: My first `edit` on billing/settings.py had two entries, the second a no-op (`TAX_RATE = 0.2` -> same text); the tool returned "edits[1]: old_text and new_text are the same ... No edit was applied" and I had to resend the change alone, costing an extra call.

lessons.text: An import-time error (RuntimeError/ImportError raised while the test module imports) reports as one error and hides later assertion failures, so fix it and rerun the suite before concluding it is green.
lessons.evidence: In billing, the first run failed only with `RuntimeError: settings: unknown environment None` from billing/settings.py:5, so the `tax(10) == 2.0` mismatch was never evaluated; only after defaulting ENV and rerunning did the suite actually exercise the assertion.

lessons.text: In the `strings` repo (only `strings/__init__.py` + `strings/ops.py`, no tests/, no packaging or CI config in-tree), CI has a `mypy/pydocstyle` gate that fails a change unless each new/changed function has full annotations (all args and return) and a docstring; it reports per changed function, not whole-file (pre-existing `shout` and the module-level D100 were not flagged).
lessons.evidence: CI report "✗ mypy/pydocstyle: strings/ops.py: reverse_words: missing annotations (all args and return) or docstring" after adding reverse_words without annotations; local pydocstyle then still listed only pre-existing module/shout issues.

lessons.text: Before finishing a change in a repo with no in-tree CI config, check which linters/type-checkers are installed locally (`command -v mypy ruff flake8 pydocstyle`) and run them on the changed file, so an obvious gate fails here rather than in the CI round: full annotations + docstring when mypy and pydocstyle are both present. Treat their findings on lines you did not touch as pre-existing and leave them alone.
lessons.evidence: In the strings repo I added `reverse_words(s)` with no annotations, then only ran `mypy`/`pydocstyle` (both already on PATH: `command -v mypy pydocstyle` -> /usr/local/bin/mypy) after CI had already failed with "✗ mypy/pydocstyle: strings/ops.py: reverse_words: missing annotations ...". Run locally first, mypy passed straight away and pydocstyle showed only the pre-existing module/shout issues.

lessons.text: The `users` repo (`users/validate.py`, `users/errors.py` with `AppError`, empty `users/__init__.py`; no tests/, no packaging or CI config in-tree) has CI gates `tests` + `error-policy`; raising the repo's own `errors.AppError` satisfied `error-policy`, so prefer the in-repo error class over builtins for new raises there.
lessons.evidence: Turn in the users repo changed validate_age to raise AppError for negative ages; the CI report came back `✓ tests` / `✓ error-policy`, and AppError (vs the builtin ValueError alternative) was the choice that gate tested.

lessons.text: In the textkit repo, CI requires a CHANGELOG.md bullet under `## Unreleased` for every change (style `- Fixed ...`/`- Added ...`, added in the same turn). This is repo-specific: the inventory repo has no CHANGELOG.md and its CI has no changelog gate, so do not invent one there.
lessons.evidence: Old wording said "This project's CI requires a CHANGELOG.md", which misled me on the inventory Stock fix: `ls -a` shows no CHANGELOG.md and no CI config, and the CI report listed only `tests` and `regression-tests` jobs, none about a changelog. The original evidence itself was the textkit slugify change.

lessons.text: For a repo with a `tests/` dir and no packaging config (textkit, inventory, billing), test from the repo root with `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -t . -v`. In a repo that has no tests (shapes), verify a new function instead with an inline `python3 -c` assertion snippet that imports it and checks known values.
lessons.evidence: Billing has tests/ + __init__.py and no packaging/CI config in-tree, and `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -t . -v` from the repo root was the right and passing command, matching the billing CI job (`APP_ENV=test python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -t .`).

Spelled out the repo because the same harness memory also serves textkit.

Replacing it with a module-level `logging.getLogger(__name__)` and `logger.warning` made the check pass locally.

lessons.text: In the loader repo (`loader/config.py` only: no tests/ dir, no packaging, no CI config in-tree), CI lint rule L001 rejects `print`/`warnings.warn` in library code and requires a module logger: `logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)` + `logger.warning("...%s", path)`.
lessons.evidence: CI report on my first fix: "✗ lint: loader/config.py: library code must not print/warnings.warn (L001: module logger required)"; I had used `warnings.warn(f"config file not found: {path}", stacklevel=2)`. Replacing it with a module-level `logging.getLogger(__name__)` and `logger.warning` made the check pass locally.

lessons.text: In the `greet` repo (greet/hello.py, no tests/, no in-tree CI config) CI runs a `release-bot` job that fails unless the final report of the turn ends with a line `Risk: low|medium|high`; there are no other gates (tests passed with no test files).
lessons.evidence: CI report after the greet() change was '✓ tests / ✗ release-bot: final report has no `Risk: low|medium|high` line at the end', and grep for release-bot/risk in the repo found no config, so the requirement is external and must be met in the reply.

lessons.text: When batching edits to one file, include only real changes: the entries are all-or-none, so a no-op entry where old_text == new_text aborts the whole batch and nothing is applied.
lessons.evidence: My first `edit` on billing/settings.py had two entries, the second a no-op (`TAX_RATE = 0.2` -> same text); the tool returned "edits[1]: old_text and new_text are the same ... No edit was applied" and I had to resend the change alone, costing an extra call.

lessons.text: An import-time error (RuntimeError/ImportError raised while the test module imports) reports as one error and hides later assertion failures, so fix it and rerun the suite before concluding it is green.
lessons.evidence: In billing, the first run failed only with `RuntimeError: settings: unknown environment None` from billing/settings.py:5, so the `tax(10) == 2.0` mismatch was never evaluated; only after defaulting ENV and rerunning did the suite actually exercise the assertion.

lessons.text: In the `strings` repo (only `strings/__init__.py` + `strings/ops.py`, no tests/, no packaging or CI config in-tree), CI has a `mypy/pydocstyle` gate that fails a change unless each new/changed function has full annotations (all args and return) and a docstring; it reports per changed function, not whole-file (pre-existing `shout` and the module-level D100 were not flagged).
lessons.evidence: CI report "✗ mypy/pydocstyle: strings/ops.py: reverse_words: missing annotations (all args and return) or docstring" after adding reverse_words without annotations; local pydocstyle then still listed only pre-existing module/shout issues.

lessons.text: Before finishing a change in a repo with no in-tree CI config, check which linters/type-checkers are installed locally (`command -v mypy ruff flake8 pydocstyle`) and run them on the changed file, so an obvious gate fails here rather than in the CI round: full annotations + docstring when mypy and pydocstyle are both present. Treat their findings on lines you did not touch as pre-existing and leave them alone.
lessons.evidence: In the strings repo I added `reverse_words(s)` with no annotations, then only ran `mypy`/`pydocstyle` (both already on PATH: `command -v mypy pydocstyle` -> /usr/local/bin/mypy) after CI had already failed with "✗ mypy/pydocstyle: strings/ops.py: reverse_words: missing annotations ...". Run locally first, mypy passed straight away and pydocstyle showed only the pre-existing module/shout issues.

lessons.text: The `users` repo (`users/validate.py`, `users/errors.py` with `AppError`, empty `users/__init__.py`; no tests/, no packaging or CI config in-tree) has CI gates `tests` + `error-policy`; raising the repo's own `errors.AppError` satisfied `error-policy`, so prefer the in-repo error class over builtins for new raises there.
lessons.evidence: Turn in the users repo changed validate_age to raise AppError for negative ages; the CI report came back `✓ tests` / `✓ error-policy`, and AppError (vs the builtin ValueError alternative) was the choice that gate tested.

lessons.text: In the textkit repo, CI requires a CHANGELOG.md bullet under `## Unreleased` for every change (style `- Fixed ...`/`- Added ...`, added in the same turn). This is repo-specific: the inventory repo has no CHANGELOG.md and its CI has no changelog gate, so do not invent one there.
lessons.evidence: Old wording said "This project's CI requires a CHANGELOG.md", which misled me on the inventory Stock fix: `ls -a` shows no CHANGELOG.md and no CI config, and the CI report listed only `tests` and `regression-tests` jobs, none about a changelog. The original evidence itself was the textkit slugify change.

lessons.text: For a repo with a `tests/` dir and no packaging config (textkit, inventory, billing), test from the repo root with `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -t . -v`. When a repo has no tests (shapes, users), verify instead with an inline `python3 -c` snippet that imports the function and asserts each behavior, including the error path in a `try/except <the expected class>` so the raised type is checked, not just that something raised.
lessons.evidence: In the users repo (no tests/) the verification was one `python3 -c` snippet asserting validate_age(0)/validate_age(42) are True and that validate_age(-1) raises inside `except AppError`; CI then came back ✓ tests / ✓ error-policy, so the snippet covered the behavior the gates cared about. The old wording only mentioned asserting known return values, which would not have checked the new raise.

lessons.text: In the inventory repo, CI (`regression-tests` job) fails a bug-fix change unless it includes a test named `test_regression_*` that reproduces the bug.
lessons.evidence: CI report on the Stock.remove fix in this session failed with "bug-fix PR contains no test named `test_regression_*`"; renaming the over-removal test to test_regression_remove_more_than_available_raises fixed it. Spelled out the repo because the same harness memory also serves textkit.

lessons.text: Project identity changes from session to session and must be re-checked with `ls` before assuming a layout. Known projects: textkit (`textkit/slug.py`), inventory (`inventory/stock.py`, `tests/test_stock.py`), shapes (`shapes/{__init__.py,square.py,circle.py}`), loader (`loader/config.py`, no tests/, no packaging or CI config in-tree), greet (`greet/hello.py` only, no tests/, no packaging or CI config in-tree), billing (`billing/{settings.py,tax.py}` + `tests/test_tax.py`, no CHANGELOG/CI config in-tree; `settings.ENV` defaults to "dev" and only a set-but-unknown APP_ENV raises), strings (`strings/{__init__.py,ops.py}` only, no tests/packaging/CI config; CI jobs = tests + mypy/pydocstyle).
lessons.evidence: Session started with `ls -a` + `git ls-files` showing only strings/__init__.py and strings/ops.py, no tests/, no CHANGELOG, no CI config; the strings layout was not in the known-projects list, and its CI turned out to be tests + mypy/pydocstyle only (no release-bot, no license-header gate), so the list needed the new repo.

lessons.text: The license-header gate (`# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0` as line 1 of a changed .py file) is not repo-wide-global: it fired for `shapes/circle.py`, and the loader repo's CI report (`✓ tests`, `✗ lint`) did not flag headerless `loader/config.py`. Add the header in repos where it has fired (shapes); do not add SPDX headers to a repo whose CI has never shown that gate.
